name: Hip Heist Wrestle-Up
keyCorrections: If you cannot get to your knees: the leg swing was too short — swing the leg wider and drive harder
If they flatten you during the hip heist: the underhook was not deep enough — re-pummel and try again
If you land in side control: you stopped at the knees instead of driving to standing
description: The Hip Heist is an explosive wrestle-up from bottom guard to stand up or take the back. It is the fastest way to go from guard to a dominant standing position.
shortInstruction: From open guard, win the underhook, swing your outside leg back, post on your hand, and drive to your knees or standing. If they follow, circle behind for the back take.
summary: The hip heist uses a hip rotation and leg swing to explosively transition from bottom guard to a kneeling or standing position. It is the highest-speed wrestle-up because it converts your hip escape momentum directly into a stand-up. The hip heist is particularly effective against opponents who lean forward with heavy pressure — their forward momentum becomes the energy you use to stand.
whyItWorks: The hip rotation creates momentum that carries you to your knees without upper body strength
The opponent's forward pressure (common in open guard passing) provides the counter-force you need to elevate
The hip heist transitions to a back take if the opponent follows your movement
It is faster than a technical stand-up and requires less space
commonMistakes: Not winning the underhook before the hip heist — without the underhook, they flatten you as you rise
Swinging the leg too wide — the leg swing must be controlled to maintain balance
Stopping at the knees instead of driving to standing — the hip heist should bring you all the way up
Telegraphing the movement — the hip heist works best when it is explosive and unexpected
coachingCues: Swing the leg, drive to standing
Follow them for the back take
safetySummary: The hip heist requires hip flexibility — do not force the leg swing if you feel hip strain
If you fail the hip heist and land flat, protect your head immediately and re-establish guard
Be careful of knee strain when driving from the hip heist to the knees — warm up properly before explosive wrestle-ups

systemLogic.corePrinciple: The hip heist wrestle-up has four phases: Underhook → Hip Rotation → Leg Swing → Stand

decisionTree.action: from open guard, win the underhook on the side you will heist. Your head should be on their chest
hip escape slightly to create space, then rotate your hips toward the mat (away from them)
swing your outside leg back and around, posting your foot on the mat. Your momentum should carry your torso upright
drive through your posted foot and the underhook to standing. If they follow the movement, circle behind for the back take

decisionTree.condition: the hip heist fails to standing
decisionTree.action: recover to a seated guard or transition to a technical stand-up

moneyDetails: The hip heist is the fastest wrestle-up in BJJ — it converts guard directly to a takedown position
Mastering the hip heist gives you a reliable stand-up from any open guard position
The hip heist to back take is a high-value transition that scores 4 points (back take) in IBJJF
fixItFast: If they pressure forward: use their momentum — hip heist in the direction they are pushing
If they back away: stand up fully and re-engage from neutral
If they try to pass during the heist: switch to a technical stand-up — it is safer against aggressive passers
